body:
Hey! You've created such an awesome plugin, such nice looking code (and there's not that much of it!). It has replaced many of my previous plugins and I am loving it. :) I have a feature request, for the surround module:

Is there a possibility of adding a `latex` "object"? It would be similar to the `special_tag` one, but with `\begin{foo}` and `\end{foo}` as left and right, rather than `<foo>`/`</foo>`.

I would have made this a PR, but I've had such little time lately that I thought I'd ask your opinion first.

Thanks!

comment_data.body:
Hello! Thanks for kind words. They mean a lot! :)

Yep, seems like a worthwhile request: useful and with (seemingly) quite compact implementation.
Played with it a bit and got it working. I have a couple of question regarding a better usage (not really a LaTeX user myself):
- I feel that adding latex surrounding to `hello` string should lead to `\begin{foo} hello \end{foo}` (with spaces around word). Is this indeed the case?
- Does inner part of `{}` always consist from alphanumeric characters? Are spaces allowed?
- Currently (and possibly forever) adding surrounding to multiple lines will lead to adding surrounding after first whitespace of the first line and before last whitespace of last line. But quick browsing of LaTeX examples showed that `\begin{}`-`\end{}` are always on separate lines and are indented. I don't think achieving this will be easy with 'mini.surround'.

More thoroughly on last point. If you linewise visually highlight these two lines (for example, with `Vip`):
```
Hello
world
```
and execute `sal` (add 'l' surrounding) supplying `document` latex object, this will lead to (assuming this also adds whitespace around textobject):
```
\begin{document} Hello
world \end{document}
```
I currently don't plan to implement and support case when this leads to:
```
\begin{document}
Hello
world
\end{document}
```
When we're at it, it would be nice to also support a "LaTeX command" surrounding (e.g. `bar` -> `\foo{bar}`).

@lupont, could you try a latex (`l`) special surrounding in `surround-latex` branch?
@xigoi, this might be a little bit more complex as this is more like "function call" surrounding, which is a little "special". But I'll see what I can do.

Wow, that was so fast! I have tried it a little and it seems to work well. I am by no means a LaTeX expert either, so if anyone reading knows something I don''t, please voice your opinion or concern!

- I personally prefer not adding spaces, as it seems less noisy to me.
- To my knowledge, `\begin{}`/`\end{}` tags are always alphanumeric.
- It's a pity that newlines/indentation are difficult - as it would really be valuable when writing LaTeX. I would argue that it's also quite useful for the `special_tag` when writing *ml. I naïvely attempted to modify the `special_latex` function by adding `\n` and `<CR>`, which obviously did not work. Would you care to share some input as to why it would be difficult/you don't plan to support it?

Thanks a lot for this!

About linewise selection, if I remember correctly, it was a combination of two reasons:
1. This behavior is more uniform. I don't think that inserting on new lines when in linewise visual selection is appropriate in case of quotes and (at least for me most of the time) parenthesis. Also it simplifies code which is frankly already kind of complicated for my taste.
2. Most of the time, when inserting surroundings on new lines, it also implies indenting the inner part. Which definitely won't be implemented here.

I understand where you're coming from. I would like to prototype the functionality for myself when I get more time on my hands. If I succeed and feel comfortable with the solution, I'll open a PR to share it with you. But I won't expect you to merge it. Thanks again!

If you are comfortable with this, sure, go ahead.
Some modules ('completion', 'surround') are already uncomfortably big and complex, and I really want to try to keep this minimal.
Hmm... Maybe some abstract "extension" mechanism in 'mini.surround' might solve this. But frankly it is not on the radar in the near future.
I imagine using uppercase versions of these kinds of operators to mean "add newlines". But that's just an initial thought without much knowledge about the code base.
Wow, awesome! I will be sure to try it out when I find some time. :) Thanks!

Thanks for this, awesome as usual. However I have some problems with both `l` and `L` above. It works flawlessly with `sa`, but not with `sd` or `sr`. Steps to reproduce what I'm saying.
1. Open a random tex file and select some text 
2. use `saLtextbf` to make the selection bold, this basically transforms `TEXT` to `\textbf{TEXT}`
3. move somewhere in `TEXT` and press `sdL` (or `srL`). 

I expected this to back from `\textbf{TEXT}` to `TEXT`, but rather it pops up `(mini.surround) Enter input surrounding identifier`, which is not what I expected, and even if I put something there I don't get the right behavior. Am I doing something wrong?

> I expected this to back from `\textbf{TEXT}` to `TEXT`, but rather it pops up `(mini.surround) Enter input surrounding identifier`, which is not what I expected, and even if I put something there I don't get the right behavior. Am I doing something wrong?

This looks like a mix of two issues here.

First one is that input surrounding specification has changed since that 3 year old comment. It is now a single [composed pattern](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4035ef97407a6661ae9ff913ff980e271a658502/doc/mini-surround.txt#L253) (which is more powerful and flexible) instead of `find` and `extract` fields. Here is [an example](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4035ef97407a6661ae9ff913ff980e271a658502/doc/mini-surround.txt#L289-L293). 

Second one is that you probably didn't press `<Shift>` and executed `sdl`. This is a ["delete previous"](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4035ef97407a6661ae9ff913ff980e271a658502/doc/mini-surround.txt#L512) action by default which will prompt user to enter surrounding identifier (so that 'mini.surround' can delete the surrounding that is located before cursor and not covering it).

I updated the suggested setup with relevant notes. I seems to work now.

Thanks, I confirm that `sd` works now, while `sr` still does not work... it deletes the surround and then asks for `output identifier`. I had no conflict, the "previous" action is set to `p` in my config. 
Another small feature request: is it possible in the `L` example to have the `{}` characters in the word (I guess in %w? I'm not familiar with lua patterns)? I often have to revise documents where people add comments like 
`\textcolor{red}{THEIR PROPOSED CHANGE}` 
and I'd like to easily get rid of the `textcolor{red}` part... No big deal though if it is too complicated, I can run a first `:%s/textcolor{red}/whatever/g` and then `sdL` once I take care of the comment. Currently this doesn't work if I press `sdL` inside `\textcolor{red}{THEIR PROPOSED CHANGE}`

> Thanks, I confirm that `sd` works now, while `sr` still does not work... it deletes the surround and then asks for `output identifier`. I had no conflict, the "previous" action is set to `p` in my config.

This is how [replace action works](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4035ef97407a6661ae9ff913ff980e271a658502/doc/mini-surround.txt#L77-L78): `sr` + `input identifier to replace` + `output identifier to replace with`. If you want to change the content of `{}`, then it will be something like `srLL` + <new content> + `<CR>`.

> Another small feature request: is it possible in the `L` example to have the `{}` characters in the word (I guess in %w? I'm not familiar with lua patterns)? I often have to revise documents where people add comments like
> `\textcolor{red}{THEIR PROPOSED CHANGE}`
> and I'd like to easily get rid of the `textcolor{red}` part... No big deal though if it is too complicated, I can run a first `:%s/textcolor{red}/whatever/g` and then `sdL` once I take care of the comment. Currently this doesn't work if I press `sdL` inside `\textcolor{red}{THEIR PROPOSED CHANGE}`

Sorry, I do not understand what is the intended outcome here. I only get that `\textcolor{red}{THEIR PROPOSED CHANGE}` is the starting point. Where do you want cursor to be placed and what is the target text you want to achieve?

> This is how [replace action works](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4035ef97407a6661ae9ff913ff980e271a658502/doc/mini-surround.txt#L77-L78): `sr` + `input identifier to replace` + `output identifier to replace with`. If you want to change the content of `{}`, then it will be something like `srLL` + + `<CR>`.
> 
I see, this totally makes sense. Thanks!

> Sorry, I do not understand what is the intended outcome here. I only get that `\textcolor{red}{THEIR PROPOSED CHANGE}` is the starting point. Where do you want cursor to be placed and what is the target text you want to achieve?

Like the previous example, but with `textcolor{red}` instead of `textbf`. For example I start with `XXXX` and press `saLtextcolor{red}` to get 
`\textcolor{red}{XXXX}` (basically making a red XXXX). This already works with your code. However, if I put the cursor under a X and press `sdL` I don't go back to `XXXX`

> Like the previous example, but with `textcolor{red}` instead of `textbf`.

Ah, I see now, my bad. Yes, this should be possible with something like `input = { [[\%S+%b{}]], '^.*{().-()}$' }`. It recognizes any non-whitespace characters before balanced `{}`.
